answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory deck, randomly select players + 1 cards face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards; one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories; randomly choose one structure bonus tile; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: Character starts at home base; two workers start one per land-adjoined territory adjoining home; four mechs start over their Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw. Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 specify mat assignments and starting pieces.

answers.answer: You must move the action token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section; otherwise sections cannot be repeated on consecutive turns. Top-row gains may pay a bottom-row cost, and the top action must precede the bottom action. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before taking as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired; exact bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section; optionally top then optionally bottom; full cost first; top-row gains may pay bottom-row cost.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay resource costs using resources on any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone controls; enemy units do not gain abilities; resources from any controlled territories may pay costs.

answers.answer: No. On a normal Move, up to two different units each move one adjacent territory; you cannot use both selections to move one unit twice. A carried worker's movement is not used up, so it may subsequently move itself. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs may carry any number of your workers, and never your character.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: two different units one territory; carried worker may subsequently move itself; all units carry resources, only mechs carry workers.

answers.answer: The Speed mech stops upon entering a territory occupied only by enemy workers, and cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat home, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero popularity does not stop the retreat. A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers only stop character/mech; workers retreat; popularity loss; worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory. Speed does not override enemy stops.

answers.answer: Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: resolve combats after finishing other unit movement and before bottom-row action; attacker chooses order. Workers cannot independently move into or out of enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discards are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity on Bolster; built Armory adds one power on Trade.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade action descriptions give costs, choices, deck exhaustion, placement, worker restriction, and building bonuses.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there produces one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village, after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps: pay in full, select territories, produce per worker; take new workers left to right after payment; may decline; new costs apply to future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box (not a solid-black-bordered red box), improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy costs metal: put any Faction Mat mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; the uncovered ability now applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay a bottom action for its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row Upgrade and Deploy descriptions; completed bottom actions may still be paid for coins and ongoing recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build costs wood and places a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents'; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill gives a bonus Produce territory and produces as one worker, even without an actual worker; it cannot produce when uncontrolled. Your Mine is a personal tunnel usable by your units even while enemy units occupy it, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions; opponents cannot use your building's ability.
answers.evidence: Build description: placement and permanence; Mill and Mine effects; Control section says uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and permanently put it on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, independent of the chosen one-time bonus. For the rest of the game, when you or your immediate left/right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right, and stop if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice. Ongoing amounts: Upgrade one power; Deploy one coin; Build one popularity; Enlist one combat card.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits sections specify placement, one-time and ongoing bonuses, order, and two-player rule.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly set dial power from zero up to the smaller of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People's Army adds one card total if any workers are present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Both players pay their dial power by deducting it from their tracks, and every played card is discarded face-up; cards do not deduct extra track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify simultaneous secret choices, card limits, ability order, reveal, payment, and attacker tie-break.

answers.answer: Winner controls territory/resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two, Saxony unrestricted within its six stars). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units/carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4–5 covers retreats, resources, attacker popularity, stars, and loser's card draw.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains on the encounter territory, discard the token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and token remains. All resources, workers, mechs, and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed option cost, but no normal action cost or mat benefits apply, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters section gives timing, contested entry, destination for gains, and exclusion of normal action costs/benefits.

answers.answer: Every player's character must, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), choose one of the available Factory cards and return the rest; each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. Use it as a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Similar Factory actions give no Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions still apply.
answers.evidence: Factory section specifies each player's first visit, card choice, later visits, action rules, and bottom Move distances.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective, and you must meet all requirements at reveal. Place its objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony keeps the other card after the first and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section specifies timing, requirements, discards, and Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops; another player's star never blocks a goal. The sixth star ends play immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end section lists achievements, permanence, goal blocking, and immediate end.

answers.answer: For a sixth star from a bottom-row action, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement portion and return initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor recruit power/popularity stars: finish the active action, then resolve active player, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star each time; if an earlier player places the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end gives bottom-action order, pending battle rollback, and neighbor bonus star sequence.

answers.answer: The example gives $20 for five stars, $21 for four ordinary territories plus Factory (seven territory units at $3 each), and $12 for 13 resources (six complete pairs at $2 each): $53 added to held coins. Structure bonus is also earned even if enemies control the territories containing your structures; score only the selected tile. Ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune example at 10 popularity; structure bonus eligibility; tiebreak order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base, with setup, forced retreats, and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare as exceptions. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases section.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources section says workers are not resources and resource tokens have no supply limit.

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, and drop off any number of resources during movement; a mech may also carry any number of your workers but never your character. Speed adds one territory to each selected character/mech, not workers; a tunnel jump costs one step, with the added step usable before or after it. A mech may pick up/drop resources and workers mid-move. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move and Speed descriptions.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: printed tunnels are adjacent for any unit; any unit may enter enemy-structure-only territory.

answers.answer: You cannot pay only part of a cost. After last using Move, you must move the token to a different section; if unable to afford any action there, you may take a dead turn by moving the token and taking neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: dead turn by moving token to a different section and taking neither action; never pay only part of a cost.

answers.answer: Armory grants one power when you take Trade; Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. You retain structure abilities even without control, and enemy units do not gain those abilities, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section on retained abilities and enemy units.

answers.answer: Riverwalk lets character/mechs cross rivers to faction-specific destinations: Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is different: it lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes, and does not help character/mechs. All five factions can unlock Speed.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities table.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine and makes the opponent lose two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery also applies before combat, but you pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two; it is once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Disarm and Artillery.

answers.answer: They may play three combat cards total: one per participating mech (two) plus one additional People's Army card because workers are present. Workers alone never fight; People's Army still requires a character/mech.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: one additional card total with workers present, still requiring a character/mech; two mechs and three workers allow three cards.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of its value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; it does not give Polania the adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off, and carried workers or resources cannot be left behind when their carrier leaves a lake.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge entries and lake-carried-unit rule.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not protect against loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Camaraderie description explicitly limits it to combat and excludes undefended-worker removal.

answers.answer: Meander allows Polania to choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first option's gain may pay the second option's cost. The summary does not state a separate procedural rule specifically requiring a second-option payment beyond the general rule that printed costs must be paid; any unaffordable option cannot be selected.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander: up to two different options in either order; first gain can pay second cost. Encounter options require printed cost and unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. The encounter resolves after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move encounter stop rule; Encounters section timing also applies during Factory Move.

answers.answer: Combat-card count is public but contents are secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but the summary says a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat players may conceal whether they committed cards until reveal.
answers.evidence: Setup information section.

answers.answer: Informal agreements are unenforceable. Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances. A payment cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units; the fight occurs after Move, though bribes may influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section.

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6, each star scores $3, territory $2, and resource pair $1; at 7–12, $4, $3, and $2; at 13–18, $5, $4, and $3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Pool controlled resources and score complete pairs only, ignoring an odd leftover.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and scoring explanation.

answers.answer: For each selected adjacency tile, count each unique qualifying feature once across all your structures. Tunnels are unique printed tunnels, not Mines; lakes are unique lakes; encounter locations are unique printed locations even if the token has been removed. Rivers do not break adjacency. Payouts for each of the three tiles (tunnels, lakes, encounters) are: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 (or 6–7 for lakes/encounters) $9. Zero scores zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table and notes: unique features, printed tunnels not Mines, removed encounter tokens count, rivers do not break adjacency.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3–4 $6. Structures in a row score only your longest continuous straight line: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Rivers do not break a straight row.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table and note that rivers do not break a straight row.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: No. A popularity star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring, so it does not protect the current amount or tier. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions can each earn a star for the same achievement.
answers.evidence: Stars section says star remains if popularity drops and other players' stars never block a goal; current popularity determines scoring.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania clockwise, omitting inactive factions. Seating determines who counts as your immediate left/right neighbor for ongoing recruit bonuses triggered by bottom-row actions.
answers.evidence: Setup mat assignment/seating and Ongoing recruits neighbor rule.

answers.answer: Rivers are borders between land hexes; lakes are entire territories adjoining surrounding shores. Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. The summary says unlocked lake abilities permit character/mechs to move to/from lakes, but does not specify which surrounding land hexes qualify as entry points; that detail is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Control section defines rivers and lakes; lake abilities state character/mechs move to/from lakes without specifying qualifying shore hexes.

answers.answer: No, the card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud; reading every option aloud is not required.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card to all players, show artwork, read capitalized thematic text; need not read every option.

answers.answer: There is no limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

answers.answer: Players may overlap a noninteractive bottom-action decision with the next turn. Interactive bonuses and game-end priority must still resolve in order. The summary does not provide a more specific universal timing point for beginning the next turn beyond this allowance.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: players may overlap a noninteractive bottom-action decision with the next turn, but resolve interactive bonuses and game-end priority in order.

answers.answer: No. A section's top action and bottom action may each be taken at most once on that turn; moving the token is required. Rusviet may repeat a section on a later turn, including Factory, but the summary does not allow repeating the action within one turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: optionally take that section's top action once and bottom action once; Rusviet may repeat a section.

answers.answer: You may take the alternative Move benefit and gain $1 instead of moving units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; workers that retreat go to home base. The summary only identifies starting Produce workers on the Player Mat and does not provide a way to return board workers to it.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to Player Mat; Move: retreating workers return home.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.
answers.evidence: Combat section: you may attack with zero power/popularity.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; the ordinary limit is two combat stars.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4: you may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.

answers.answer: Normally you choose one affordable option; you must pay its printed cost, so an unaffordable coin/popularity option cannot be selected. You may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired. The summary does not explicitly say whether a faction without Meander may choose no option at all, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Encounters: normally choose one affordable option, must pay printed cost, may take as little benefit as desired; explicit no-option choice is not addressed.

answers.answer: No. Combatants choose their dials simultaneously and secretly, rather than in turn order. They reveal simultaneously after selecting any combat cards.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: simultaneously and secretly choose, then reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: No. Stars are placed as soon as achieved and the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it, on your own turn before or after a top/bottom action.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved, sixth ends immediately. Objectives: may wait to reveal completed objective.

answers.answer: No. By default units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; unlocked abilities give exceptions.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is permanently placed on the one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit put permanently on bonus; it cannot later move.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; its entry stops further movement and the encounter is resolved later if it remains there.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter.

answers.answer: A controlled Mill provides an additional bonus Produce territory, so you may choose it in addition to up to two different controlled territories (three total). The Mill itself produces as one worker, even with no actual worker there, as long as it is controlled.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill provides an additional bonus territory and itself produces as one worker; uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.

answers.answer: A territory is controlled if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure, resources there do not preserve your control. An enemy worker alone on your structure territory controls it and its resources.
answers.evidence: Control definition; resources are not listed as establishing control.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row resources: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal; Build—wood; Enlist—food.
